correctness.rationale: For every base edge, its line-graph neighbor-one count equals the sum of the two endpoint incidence counts minus twice the edge bit. The equal-parity assumption yields an integral critical value and exact three-way update. On a two-cycle, each changing edge contributes a nonpositive term delta_e(Delta_u+Delta_v), whereas their sum equals the nonnegative sum of vertex-incidence-change squares. Hence all Delta vanish. The factor characterization is proved in both directions, and the orbit-count coefficient counts each periodic state exactly once, pairing distinct states of each primitive two-cycle. Standalone Python and C++ replays checked all 154 eligible simple base graphs on at most five vertices (4,909 eligible states) and selected larger graphs including all 2,097,152 states on L(K7); these are finite corroboration rather than an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The finite-graph eventual-period-two theorem is explicitly credited to Goles and Olivos. The result proved here adds incidence-degree conservation for all parity-homogeneous base graphs and an if-and-only-if half-factor decomposition of recurrent states on line graphs. The inspected primary majority-dynamics paper gives period bounds and broad convergence/disagreement results, not this structure. Targeted literature, published research-record, and accessible own-record implication searches found no stronger statement that yields the classification. Full access to the 1980 original was unavailable, so this is a best-knowledge review, not a uniqueness certification.
residual_risks: The original Goles–Olivos (1980) full text was inaccessible in authorized retrieval; a line-graph specialization in its body cannot be ruled out solely from the abstract.
A historically unindexed result may express the same theorem as edge-color majority, a balanced factor condition, or threshold-network conservation.
Semantic search and string search do not prove novelty; independent literature review remains valuable.

value.rationale: The result supplies a nontrivial structural invariant of every two-cycle on a broad class of line graphs, a complete necessary-and-sufficient recurrent-state classification, an exact factor-enumerator orbit formula, and Eulerian/bridge restrictions. This determines oscillating supports rather than merely bounding temporal periods. The joined-odd-triangles example shows the factor condition has content beyond the standard even-cycle intuition. Such information is suited to recurrence and graph-factor analyses on arbitrary finite regular networks; no efficient counting or transient claim is assumed.
